title: “Il cielo in una stanza” by Mina
text: "Il cielo in una stanza" is a song written by Gino Paoli and originally recorded by Italian singer Mina for the album of the same name. The song was released as a single in June 1960 by Italdisc.
listen: Il cielo in una stanza Mina

title: “What a Sky (Su nel cielo)” by Nico Fidenco
text: Domenico Colarossi known professionally as Nico Fidenco, was an Italian singer and film soundtrack composer who gained considerable popularity in 1960 with the release of the song "What a Sky" (Italian: "Su nel cielo"), taken from the film Silver Spoon Set by Francesco Maselli. Self-taught in music, Fidenco did a few cover versions of film title songs for the Italian market.
listen: What a Sky (Su nel cielo) Nico Fidenco

title: “24.000 baci” by Adriano Celentano
text: "24.000 baci", also spelled as "24 mila baci", is a 1961 song composed by Ezio Leoni, Piero Vivarelli, Lucio Fulci, and Adriano Celentano. The song premiered at the 11th edition of the Sanremo Music Festival with a double performance of Adriano Celentano and Little Tony, and placed second.

title: “Come sinfonia” by Pino Donaggio
text: "Come sinfonia" is a 1961 Italian song composed by Pino Donaggio. The song premiered at the 11th edition of the Sanremo Music Festival, with a double performance by Donaggio and Teddy Reno, and placed at the sixth place.

title: “Jealous of You” by Connie Francis
text: "Everybody's Somebody's Fool" is a song written by Jack Keller and Howard Greenfield that was a No. 1 hit for Connie Francis in 1960.

title: “Where the Boys Are”
text: Where the Boys Are is a 1960 American CinemaScope romantic comedy film directed by Henry Levin and starring Dolores Hart, George Hamilton, Yvette Mimieux, Jim Hutton, Barbara Nichols, Paula Prentiss, Frank Gorshin, and Connie Francis. The screenplay by George Wells is based on the 1960 novel of the same name by Glendon Swarthout.

title: “La novia” by Domenico Modugno
text: "La novia" is a popular song by Chilean songwriter Joaquín Prieto, first recorded by his brother Antonio Prieto. Recorded in Mexico, it became an instant hit in that country and the brothers' native Chile.

title: “Pepito” by Los Machucambos
text: Los Machucambos was a music band formed in Paris in 1959. The two guitar players were Rafael Gayoso, Milton Zapata (from Peru) and the singer was Julia Cortés (from Costa Rica) .

title: “Nata per me” by Adriano Celentano
text: "Nata per me" is a song by Italian singer Adriano Celentano. Released in 1961, it was the number one hit on the Italian Hit Parade Singles Chart for a total of 12 weeks between November 1961 and 1962.

title: “La ballata della tromba” by Nini Rosso
text: Raffaele Celeste "Nini" Rosso was an Italian jazz trumpeter and composer.
